content: Valerian, when used in combination with certain medications, can lead to significant pharmacodynamic interactions, primarily by increasing sedation or central nervous system (CNS) depression. Below are the specific interactions and recommendations: 1. Valerian and Oxycodone: Both substances increase sedation. It is advised to avoid this combination or use an alternative drug. 2. Valerian and Oxymorphone: Both increase sedation. Avoid or consider alternative medications. 3. Valerian and Pancuronium: Both enhance sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 4. Valerian and Paroxetine: Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Valerian and Pentazocine: Both increase sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 6. Valerian and Pentobarbital: Valerian enhances the effects of pentobarbital through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 7. Valerian and Pexidartinib: Valerian increases the levels or effects of pexidartinib, which is a UGT substrate. If co-administration is unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose and refer to dosage modification guidelines. After discontinuing the UGT inhibitor, the previous pexidartinib dose may be resumed after three elimination half-lives. 8. Valerian and Phenelzine: Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 9. Valerian and Phenobarbital: Valerian enhances the effects of phenobarbital through pharmacodynamic synergy, potentially increasing CNS depression. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 10. Valerian and Primidone: Valerian increases the effects of primidone through pharmacodynamic synergy, potentially enhancing CNS depression. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Valerian and Promethazine: Valerian enhances the effects of promethazine through pharmacodynamic synergy, increasing CNS depression. Use caution and monitor closely. 12. Valerian and Protriptyline: Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Valerian and Quazepam: Both increase sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 14. Valerian and Ramelteon: Both increase sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 15. Valerian and Remifentanil: Both increase sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 16. Valerian and Rocuronium: Both increase sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 17. Valerian and Ropeginterferon Alfa-2b: Both may increase neuropsychiatric side effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug, and monitor for excessive CNS toxicity. 18. Valerian and Sertraline: Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Valerian and Succinylcholine: Both increase sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 20. Valerian and Sufentanil (including sublingual formulations): Both increase sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Valerian and Suvorexant: Both increase sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 22. Valerian and Tapentadol: Both increase sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 23. Valerian and Tasimelteon: Both increase sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 24. Valerian and Temazepam: Both increase sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 25. Valerian and Tramadol: Both increase sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 26. Valerian and Tranylcypromine: Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 27. Valerian and Triazolam: Both increase sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 28. Valerian and Triclofos: Valerian enhances the effects of triclofos through pharmacodynamic synergy, potentially increasing CNS depression. Use caution and monitor closely. 29. Valerian and Trimipramine: Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 30. Valerian and Triprolidine: Valerian enhances the effects of triprolidine through pharmacodynamic synergy, potentially increasing CNS depression. Use caution and monitor closely. 31. Valerian and Vecuronium: Both increase sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 32. Valerian and Venlafaxine: Both increase sedation. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Valerian and Zaleplon: Both increase sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 34. Valerian and Zolpidem: Both increase sedation. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 35. Valerian and Zuranolone: Both enhance each other’s effects through pharmacodynamic synergy, potentially increasing CNS depression and impairing psychomotor performance. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If co-administration is unavoidable, consider dose reduction. Additional Considerations: Pregnancy and Lactation: Valerian use is not recommended during pregnancy or lactation due to insufficient safety data. Chronic Use: Long-term use of valerian may lead to withdrawal symptoms. Adverse Effects: Potential side effects include cardiac disturbances, excitability, headache, hepatotoxicity, insomnia, morning drowsiness, sedation, uneasiness, and withdrawal syndrome. CNS Depressants: Concurrent use of valerian with other CNS depressants, narcotics, hypnotics, or sedatives may result in additive neuropsychiatric side effects. Patients should be closely monitored for excessive CNS toxicity. In summary, valerian has significant interactions with numerous medications, primarily increasing sedation or CNS depression. In most cases, it is recommended to avoid these combinations or use alternative therapies. If co-administration is unavoidable, close monitoring and dose adjustments are necessary.
